title: Prudent Corporate Advisory Services Ltd - 543527 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Prudent Q4 FY26: record ₹4,300 crore quarterly equity net sales offset MTM hit; AUM rebounded to ₹1.33 trillion by 5 May 2026.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 average AUM rose 0.3% QoQ to ₹1,28,000 crore and 26% YoY despite a 14.5% market fall, helped by record quarterly equity net sales of ₹4,300 crore. Closing equity AUM fell 8.2% QoQ to ₹1,15,480 crore on ₹14,550 crore of mark-to-market losses. Revenue grew 5.1% QoQ and operating profit 19.5% QoQ, but PAT growth slowed to 2.6% QoQ because other income turned negative (₹-4.7 crore). Management flagged two regulatory items for FY27: SEBI's TER change (GST now inside the expense ratio) and withdrawal of the 5 bps exit-load benefit, with industry clarity expected by end-May.

financial_highlights.change: Below FY26 average AUM of ₹1.21 trillion
MTM loss of 11.6% vs NIFTY 500 about 14%
+₹209 crore over 12 months; market share 3.65% vs 3.45% in Dec 2025
In line with 21.7% average AUM growth; yield stable at 91 bps
Health fresh premium +35%, life fresh premium +28%; Q4 insurance revenue +69% QoQ
Q4 PAT +2.6% QoQ; other income -₹4.7 crore vs +₹9.5 crore in Q3
Highest ever; Q4 ₹4,300 crore highest-ever quarter

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: FY26 MF revenue +21% in line with average AUM growth; yield held at 91 bps for three years. Equity net sales ₹13,900 crore (record); SIP book ₹1,188 crore per month.

segments.name: Insurance
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue +18% against fresh premium growth of 35% (health) and 28% (life), with revenue softened by health commission cuts from 1 Oct 2025 after GST went to nil. Term-plus-ULIP is now the largest life category.

segments.name: Other financial products
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹33 crore: ₹22 crore PMS, ₹6 crore FD, rest small-case/LAS; about 34-35% growth excluding discontinued LiquiLoans (₹6.7 crore last year). SIF flows about ₹90 crore in Q4, running at ₹25-30 crore per month now.

segments.name: Indus Capital (acquired)
segments.commentary: AUM ₹2,250 crore currently, up from ₹2,060 crore at end-September 2025 and ₹2,085 crore at acquisition; full team retained.

guidance_outlook: Employee cost for existing base expected to rise about 14% in FY27; monthly salary bill ₹8.93 crore (Mar 2026) to ₹10.2 crore (Apr 2026); 1,540 employees at 31 Mar 2026.
Other income: ₹11.5 crore current MTM gain on MF portfolio; management expects a healthy other-income contribution by 30 June 2026 if markets hold.
Book yield impact from exit-load pass-on estimated at 2-3 bps on the entire AUM; new-business yield expected broadly neutral.
Net yield expected to stay positive and overall book yield to remain static, with 1-1.5 bps (or ~2 bps) possible movement in April on the total book.
ESOP cost guided at ~₹7 crore this year; ~₹8.5 crore next year, a ballpark figure not approved by the board.
Gross sales of ₹30,000-35,000 crore expected in FY27 on AUM of ₹1,30,000 crore.
Industry clarity on the 5 bps exit-load withdrawal expected by end of May 2026.
capex_capacity: Fundzbazar AI platform: Prudent Edge (for MFDs) and FundzEdge (for retail) launched in beta mode; partner feedback to be tracked over the next few months.
Treasury investments ₹585 crore, of which ₹200 crore parked in Balance Advantage Fund and hybrid SIFs.
Acquisitions described as an ongoing work in process with no concrete deal; management declined to give a timeline.
demand_pricing: Q4 gross flows were lump-sum heavy: lump sum about ₹5,300 crore vs SIP stable; management says the long-run mix is about 50:50, and March flows were only about ₹100 crore above Jan-Feb.
Top 5 AMCs about 50% of AUM; channel mix about 90:10 B2B2C vs direct plus Indus; new flows about 93-94% B2B2C.
Non-GST distributors face 15-20% revenue impact from TER/GST changes; management says Prudent is about 15% more competitive versus AMC rates for them.
Management estimates 15-16% of AUM sits with non-GST-registered partners (unverified, per market talk).
Life insurance ULIP sales up about 5-6% YoY, which dilutes yield; yield otherwise maintained post-October.
SIF margins in line with mutual funds; about 6,000 industry distributors certified and over 1,000 with Prudent.
Insurance yield expected to fall this year as regulator rationalises commissions.
Competition from new B2B2C platforms seen as not yet materially hurting flows; 5,100 new partners added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the fee and commission expense ratio lower in Q4, and is it Indus-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a nil additional trail provision in Q4 (₹5.5 crore in Q3) plus about ₹4.5 crore of insurance revenue recognised in March, about ₹10 crore extra revenue in total. Full-year commission figures were said to be more representative.

qa_highlights.question: How will the exit-load pass-on and GST-driven TER change affect distributor payouts and yields?
qa_highlights.answer: New business yield expected broadly neutral; book impact 2-3 bps, pending clarity from a couple of AMCs. Payouts will be realigned net of GST, with the April calculation still pending, so the monetary impact cannot yet be quantified.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 'lump sum' share of flows persist if markets recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lump sum is typically higher in corrections and the long-run mix is around 50:50; a market downturn would shift mix toward SIPs over time.

qa_highlights.question: Is SIP market share (3.5-3.7%) being lost to other platforms or direct?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct share is rising industry-wide. Prudent says it is gaining regular-plan share and rising monthly by a few bps, but it does not target a specific share level.

qa_highlights.question: What share of MFD AUM is held by larger distributors, and does leakage occur after scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no AUM share; 2,220 MFDs have crossed ₹10 crore AUM. No MFD has left after reaching ₹100 crore, per management; 40-50% of joiners are new to the industry.

qa_highlights.question: Indus AUM retention and further acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Indus AUM has grown from ₹2,060 crore (Sept 2025) to ₹2,250 crore with the full team retained. Further acquisitions are being scouted but nothing is concrete.

risks_watch: Exit-load (5 bps) and GST-related TER changes: final book impact (2-3 bps estimated) depends on a couple of AMCs not yet communicating; industry clarity expected by end-May 2026.
Other income volatility: Q4 other income of -₹4.7 crore; treasury sensitivity to markets (₹585 crore treasury book).
SIP cancellations rose in FY26 and new SIP registrations dipped post-February; sustainability depends on market returns.
Insurance commission rationalisation and ULIP mix may further pressure life and health yields in FY27.
Competitive intensity from new B2B2C platforms and non-GST distributors shifting to platforms; watch SIP market share (3.65% in March).
summary.management_tone: Confident on the business and AUM rebound, but guarded and often non-committal on regulatory impacts, pending AMC clarity and the payout calculation. Management repeatedly declined to give blended yield, market share or acquisition targets.
key_quotes: The good news is that we have bounced back strongly. Our AUM as of 5th May has already climbed to 1.33 trillion.
Our equity net sales at INR 13,900 crore were the highest ever in the history.
Persistency is still the highest. I think still we are maintaining more than 94%-95% of persistency.
Overall, my yield should not come under any compression because on the book, other than GST, we might see a 2-3 basis point impact

growth.why: Management guides FY27 gross MF sales of ₹30,000-35,000 crore on ₹1,30,000 crore AUM and ~14% employee cost growth, backed by record ₹4,300 crore Q4 equity net sales and a rising SIP book, but no capacity additions and no revenue growth % guided.
